cards.text: Friend, King David had fighters so legendary that the Bible writes down their names. These are David's mighty men, and up first is Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite, chief of the Three. I've been practicing that name all week, and my mustache STILL trips over it.

cards.question: Josheb-basshebeth picks up his spear. How many men does he take on, all at one time?

cards.text: EIGHT HUNDRED at one time, and I lose fights with a bag of chocolate chips. Next in command is Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men, who goes with David to taunt the Philistines gathered for battle at Pas-dammim.

cards.question: True or false: When the fight starts at Pas-dammim, the men of Israel charge in right beside Eleazar.

cards.text: The men of Israel retreat, backing away like they all just remembered they left an oven on at home.

cards.question: Israel's troops are pulling back from the Philistines. What does Eleazar do?

cards.text: Eleazar stands his ground and strikes the Philistines until his hand grows weary and sticks to his sword. Baker, after a double batch, my mustache stays curled around the whisk for an HOUR.

cards.question: After a day like that, the passage says ___ brought about a great victory.
Then Israel's troops finally come back to Eleazar. What do they come back for?

cards.text: They skip the whole fight and show up for the spoils, like coworkers who dodge the project and then show up for the cookie box. And after Eleazar comes Shammah son of Agee the Hararite.
The Philistines band together near a field full of lentils, and Israel's troops flee from them.

cards.question: Israel's troops have fled from the Philistines near the lentil field. Where does Shammah take his stand?

answers.text: In the middle of the field
At the edge of the camp

cards.question: True or false: Shammah defends the lentil field, but the Philistines take it from him in the end.

cards.text: Shammah defends that field and strikes down the Philistines, and the LORD brings about a great victory. One man holds a whole field, and I can't even defend the last cookie in the box from MYSELF.
Now here's a story from harvest time. Three of the thirty chief men go down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines is camped in the Valley of Rephaim.

cards.question: David is in the stronghold. Where do the Philistines have a garrison at this time?

cards.text: Then David longs for water, and he says it out loud: "Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!"

cards.question: The Philistines are holding Bethlehem, and David just wished out loud for its water. What do the three mighty men do?

answers.text: Break through the Philistine camp for it
Tell David it's too risky to try
Wait for the Philistines to pull out

cards.text: They break through the Philistine camp, draw water from that well and bring it back to David. That's like you sighing "I wish I had my phone charger," and three coworkers drive through rush hour to go get it.

cards.question: True or false: David drinks the water his three mighty men brought him.
David refuses to drink the water from Bethlehem. What does he do with it instead?

answers.text: Pours it out to the LORD
Gives it back to the three
Saves it for the next battle

cards.question: David pours the water out to the LORD. Why won't he drink it?

answers.text: To him it's the blood of men who risked their lives
He's afraid the Philistines poisoned the well
He wants to wait until the battle is won

cards.text: David says, "Far be it from me, O LORD, to do this! Is this not the blood of the men who risked their lives?" Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.

Back to the honor roll, friend. Now meet Abishai son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, who's over David's army (2 Samuel 8:16). Abishai is called chief of the Three too, and he's got a spear of his own.

cards.question: Abishai wields his spear against a crowd of men and kills them. How many?

cards.text: Three hundred, and Abishai wins a name along with the Three. Then the passage asks, "Was he not more honored than the Three?"

cards.question: True or false: Abishai becomes the commander of the Three.

cards.text: Abishai is their commander, even though he's not included among the Three. That's like being made admin of a group chat you were never added to.
Next up is Benaiah son of Jehoiada, a man of valor from Kabzeel and a man of many exploits. He strikes down two champions of Moab, and then, on a snowy day, he goes down into a pit.

cards.question: On a snowy day, Benaiah goes down into a pit and kills a ___.

cards.text: A snowy day, a pit AND a lion, and I hit snooze when the kitchen's a little chilly. Then Benaiah faces an Egyptian, a huge man with a spear in his hand.

cards.question: True or false: Benaiah takes on the huge Egyptian with a spear of his own.
Benaiah goes at the spear-holding Egyptian with just a club. How does he win?

answers.text: Snatches the spear and uses it on him
Knocks him down with the club
Calls in the guard to finish it

cards.text: Benaiah snatches the spear right out of the Egyptian's hand, kills him with it, and wins a name along with the three mighty men. He showed up with a club and went home with an UPGRADE.

cards.question: True or false: With all those exploits, Benaiah becomes one of the Three.
Benaiah is the most honored among the Thirty, but not one of the Three. What does David put him over?

cards.text: Then comes the list of the Thirty, men from all over, starting with Asahel, Joab's brother, and even including an Ammonite and a man from Zobah. The very last name is Uriah the Hittite, Bathsheba's husband, the man David told Joab to put at the front of the fiercest battle so he would be killed (2 Samuel 11:3, 15). Thirty-seven in all.

findings.problem: "King David had fighters so legendary that the Bible writes down their names" gives a reason the names are recorded. The text only says "These are the names of David's mighty men" (2 Samuel 23:8) and gives no reason.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but the wrong answers "At the edge of the camp" and "Up on a hill nearby" are generic spots. They are not real details from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: Four of the five choice cards in this stop are multiple choice (cards 2, 4, 7 and 8). There is one true or false and no fill in the blank, so one type dominates the stop.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The right answer "To him it's the blood of men who risked their lives" is noticeably longer than both wrong answers, and its wording echoes the verse. That makes it stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences. It is not the walkthrough's opening card, so it should have one or two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Abishai is called chief of the Three too" gives away card 4. Card 4 asks the baker to mark true or false that Abishai becomes the commander of the Three, and "chief of the Three" means nearly the same thing.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "He strikes down two champions of Moab, and then, on a snowy day, he goes down into a pit" puts the two exploits in order. Verse 20 lists them without saying which came first.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: "Then Benaiah faces an Egyptian" puts this exploit after the lion. Verse 21 says "He also struck down an Egyptian," which adds another exploit to the list without placing it in time.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Many choice cards can only be answered by luck. A baker can't reason out the right pick from the earlier cards on Stop 1 cards 2, 4 and 9, Stop 2 cards 2, 6 and 7, or Stop 3 cards 2, 7 and 9. That is close to half of the 19 choice cards, which is more than a few. Some of these, like Stop 1 card 4 and Stop 2 card 6, could get more context on the story card before them.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
